question.text: Mr. Rajesh Khanna, an individual, seeks accreditation to qualify as an Accredited Investor for investing in 'Chenab AI-Only Fund'. Under SEBI's Accredited Investor framework, he qualifies if:

answer.text: His annual income is at least INR 50 lakh

His annual income is at least INR 2 crore; OR net worth at least INR 7.5 crore with INR 3.75 crore in financial assets; OR income INR 1 crore and net worth INR 5 crore with INR 2.5 crore in financial assets
He has been investing in the securities market for at least 10 years, regardless of income
His net worth is at least INR 25 crore including primary residence

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Per SEBI's Accredited Investor Framework: for individuals/HUFs/sole proprietorships/partnerships, eligibility requires EITHER (a) annual income >= INR 2 crore, OR (b) net worth >= INR 7.5 crore with >= INR 3.75 crore in financial assets, OR (c) annual income >= INR 1 crore AND net worth >= INR 5 crore with >= INR 2.5 crore in financial assets. Primary residence value is EXCLUDED from net-worth computation for individuals, HUF Kartas and sole proprietors. **The Trap:** Option A (INR 50 lakh) is too low. Option C invents an experience-based test. Option D includes primary residence which is expressly excluded and uses the body-corporate figure. **Cross-Exam Context:** XIX-A/B have brief AI mentions. XIX-C requires precise tripartite test. Also tested in XXI-A/B (PMS) where AI thresholds differ slightly in application. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** Manager tip: At onboarding, collect the Accreditation Certificate (bearing unique accreditation number, PAN, validity) AND an AI Consent Undertaking. AI accreditation validity: 2 years for one-year eligibility; 3 years for two-year consistent eligibility. AI status is locked-in for the scheme's life even if the investor loses AI status mid-tenure.
